Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson's team-record streak of consecutive field goals made ended at 25, with a miss on a 43-yard attempt during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium.
 It was McPherson's first field-goal miss of the season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McPherson made a 24-yarder in the first quarter.
 McPherson made a pair of field goals, including one from 57 yards, during the Bengals' NFL Week 9 win against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain.

(Phil Didion/The Enquirer) McPherson made a 26-yard field goal to break the franchise record for most consecutive field goals converted with 22, during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 5 win against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.
 Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson (2) walks off after a 43-yard miss ended his team-record streak at 25 in the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 15, 2026 at Paycor Stadium. (Sam Greene/ The Enquirer) McPherson's streak dated back to Week 11 of the 2025 season. He broke the record held by Shayne Graham, who made 21 consecutive FGs in 2007.
 McPherson was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McPherson converted each of his eight field-goal attempts and eight extra points over the Bengals' three games in September.
 McPherson 's 32 points scored in September tied for the most by any NFL kicker, while his FG total tied for the most by an AFC kicker. McPherson also led all kickers in FGs made from 50 or more yards (five).
 McPherson is in his sixth NFL season, all with the Bengals.
 In 2025, McPherson broke his own record for longest field goal in team history with a 63-yarder to end the first half of the Week 12 loss to New England at Paycor Stadium.
 McPherson's kick was one of 14 field goals in NFL history of at least 63 yards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement McPherson attempted a 67-yard field goal at the end of the first half of the team's NFL Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. He made the attempt , but it didn't count. The Packers called timeout, and the whistle blew to negate what would have been an NFL record.
 McPherson played in 12 games during the 2024 season , missing time because of a groin injury.
